title: Mordheim KB catalogue — hired-sword profiles of catalog/hirelings/hired-swords
description: The canonical identity of a Hired Sword: what belongs to the warrior himself — characteristics, intrinsic equipment, skill access, starting skills, intrinsic rules and his contribution to the warband rating. The campaign-side contract (hiring fee, upkeep, availability and eligibility) lives in `catalog/campaign/hired-swords-and-dramatis.yaml`, which points back here through `profile_id`; a hired sword therefore never repeats its fee or its hiring restrictions in this file.

catalog.description: Catalogue id shared by every grade file of the family: `hirelings-hired-swords`.

grade.description: Grade of the file. `core` is the Mordheim Rulebook roster; `1a`, `1b`, `1c`, `2a` and `2b` are the fan and supplement grades, kept apart so a source change stays auditable.

rules.description: The rules of the profiles of the core file. The core roster declares its rules here, with `source_refs`, and its profiles point at them with `rule_ids`; the fan grades keep the rules inline in the profile instead.

catalog_rule.description: A rule declared by the document itself and referenced by a profile's `rule_ids`.

kind.description: Optional editorial classification. `special-skill-option` marks an entry that `special_skill_rule_ids` offers as an optional skill rather than a rule the profile always has.

mechanics.description: Optional typed mechanics the rule declares, e.g. the Ogre Butcher's effect on the maximum number of models.

mechanic.description: A mechanically typed value a rule declares, e.g. `{ type: warband.maximum_models_modifier, value: 1 }`.

profile.description: One Hired Sword. Its rules are inline (`rules`) or shared (`rule_ids`) — never duplicated in both.

grade.description: Grade of the profile; it repeats the file's grade so a record keeps its source when moved.

publication.description: Publication the profile was printed in, e.g. `Mordheim Rulebook` or `Town Cryer 13`.

experience.description: Starting Experience the profile begins with, when the source grants any. It is the field a band profile carries (`profiles.yaml`), under the same name and with the same meaning, so a veteran Hired Sword keeps his starting advance count. Absent when the profile starts at zero, which is the common case.

warband_rating.description: The rating a Hired Sword contributes. It is either a fixed value, or a base plus one point per accumulated Experience point.

equipment.description: Intrinsic equipment: what the profile comes with. A choice records the printed alternative instead of duplicating catalogue items.

skill_access.description: Skill lists the profile may learn from: `combat`, `shooting`, `academic`, `strength`, `speed`, `special` and the `cavalry` list used by mounted profiles.

starting_skill_ids.description: Canonical skill ids the profile starts with. Empty when the source declares none — the key is never dropped, so `no skills` is stated rather than implied.

rules.description: The intrinsic special rules, inline: text that belongs to this profile and is not shared with another one.

rule_ids.description: Ids of rules that live in `hired-swords/rules.yaml` or in this file. A profile uses this list instead of repeating shared prose in `rules`.

special_skill_rule_ids.description: Ids of the optional special skills the profile may pick, e.g. `hireling.hired-sword.dwarf-troll-slayer.skill.ferocious-charge`.

unresolved_references.description: Source concepts this profile uses whose canonical catalogue does not exist yet. Never given a guessed canonical id; each entry names the kind of gap and the source wording, and disappears when the catalogue lands. An empty list is the declared convention for `nothing pending`.

source_notes.description: Editorial notes about the transcription: a label typo kept out of the data, an editorial recommendation not printed in the original, a source disagreement.

normalization_status.description: Editorial state of the profile. Every published Hired Sword of this family is `normalized`; a profile that cannot be modelled is not published here but in the Dramatis catalogue, with its `out_of_scope_reason`.

kind.description: `fixed` for a flat contribution; `base_plus_experience` for a base amount plus one point per Experience point.

per_experience_point.description: Points added per accumulated Experience point, when `kind` is `base_plus_experience`.

equipment.description: Intrinsic equipment of a profile. Every key is optional so a profile without equipment states the absence by omission, and an empty list is not needed.

optional_items.description: Items the profile may take under a named condition, e.g. the mount rules of an optional warhorse.

unique_equipment.description: Equipment that exists only on this profile: named here with its own rules instead of being invented as a catalogue item.

fixed_item.description: A canonical item with the quantity the profile carries.

item_id.description: Canonical `item_id` of `catalog/items/`. Existing ids are referenced, never duplicated.

notes.description: Editorial note on the reference, not on the item: how the source's wording resolves to this canonical id (`Harpoon gun counts as harpoon crossbow`), or what the printed entry says about carrying it. The same field the band equipment lists carry on their entries.

optional_item.description: A canonical item the profile may take when a named condition holds.

when.description: Condition under which the item may be taken.

unique_equipment.description: A piece of equipment that exists only on this profile. Its id follows the profile (`hireling.hired-sword.<slug>.item.<slug>`) so it can be referenced by the profile's rules.

counts_as.description: Canonical item this equipment counts as, either named plainly or with the context in which it counts as it.

save.description: Save the equipment grants, as printed: `4+`, or `4+ unmodifiable` when the source forbids modifiers.

rules.description: Ids of the rules of this same profile that describe the equipment.

counts_as.description: Canonical item this unique equipment counts as, in a named context.

context.description: Where it counts as that item: `rules` or `close_combat`.

choice.description: A printed choice: how many options are picked, and the options themselves.

choose.description: How many options the player picks.

choice_option.description: One option of a choice: a concrete loadout, or a pick from a list of items.

choose_items.description: How many items are picked from `from_item_ids`.

repetition_allowed.description: Whether the same item may be picked more than once.

inline_rule.description: A rule that belongs to one profile. Its id follows the profile (`hireling.hired-sword.<slug>.rule.<slug>`); a rule shared by several profiles is promoted to `rules.yaml` instead.

kind.description: Optional editorial classification of the rule.

mechanics.description: Optional typed mechanics the rule declares.

unresolved_reference.description: A source concept with no canonical catalogue yet.

source_name.description: The wording of the source, kept verbatim so the concept can be recognised when its catalogue lands.

note.description: Why it is unresolved, when the source wording alone does not say.
